name: OpenTodo
summary: A self-hostable, offline-capable to-do app with shared projects, time blocking, focus timers and optional end-to-end encryption.
use_cases: add tasks in plain language with date, project and priority
time-block tasks on a day or week calendar
share projects with family or a team
import tasks from Todoist, TickTick or Things
features: quick add tasks in natural language
plan the day with time blocking

manual_steps: Open http://localhost:8080 in a browser to create the first account

steps.command: mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && cd ~/.local/bin && curl -fsSLO https://github.com/OpenTodoApp/OpenTodo/releases/download/v1.5.0/opentodo-linux-amd64 && curl -fsSLO https://github.com/OpenTodoApp/OpenTodo/releases/download/v1.5.0/ot-linux-amd64 && curl -fsSLO https://github.com/OpenTodoApp/OpenTodo/releases/download/v1.5.0/SHA256SUMS && sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS && mv opentodo-linux-amd64 opentodo && mv ot-linux-amd64 ot && chmod +x opentodo ot
steps.purpose: Download opentodo-linux-amd64 and ot-linux-amd64 v1.5.0 release binaries to ~/.local/bin, verify SHA256SUMS, rename and chmod +x

linux.first_task: ot add "Call Sarah next Wed 3pm #work p1" --natural --json

setup.command:
set -e
B=http://127.0.0.1:8080
curl -sSf -c /tmp/cj -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"owner@example.com","name":"Owner","password":"Kq7vXp2mLw9zRt4nB8"}' $B/api/v1/auth/register
echo
curl -sSf -b /tmp/cj -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"cli"}' $B/api/v1/tokens | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["secret"])' > /tmp/tok
ot auth set-token "$(cat /tmp/tok)" --server $B
cat > /tmp/f2.sh <<'EOF'
set -e
B=http://127.0.0.1:8080; T=$(cat /tmp/tok)
curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"title\":\"Write report\",\"due\":{\"date\":\"$(date +%F)\",\"time\":\"10:00\"},\"estimate_minutes\":90}" $B/api/v1/tasks
echo
ot today
EOF
cat > /tmp/f3.sh <<'EOF'
set -e
B=http://127.0.0.1:8080; T=$(cat /tmp/tok)
ID=$(ot add "Deep work session")
ot time log "$ID" 25m --note pomodoro
curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" "$B/api/v1/time-entries?task=$ID"
echo
EOF
cat > /tmp/f4.sh <<'EOF'
set -e
B=http://127.0.0.1:8080; T=$(cat /tmp/tok)
PID=$(curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Family"}' $B/api/v1/projects | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])')
INV=$(curl -sSf -b /tmp/cj -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"role":"editor"}' $B/api/v1/projects/$PID/invites)
echo "$INV"
S=$(echo "$INV" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["link"].rstrip("/").split("/")[-1])')
curl -sSf -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"email\":\"member@example.com\",\"name\":\"Member\",\"password\":\"Zr5tQm8wPx3nLk6vY2\",\"projectInvite\":\"$S\"}" $B/api/v1/auth/register
echo
curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" $B/api/v1/projects/$PID/members
echo
EOF
ot project add work

pitfalls.readme_said: To build from source: make build && ./bin/opentodo (Go 1.26+ and Node 22+)
pitfalls.actually_needed: I used the prebuilt opentodo-linux-amd64 release binary, which the README's Single binary section offers, because this box cannot install a Go toolchain

pitfalls.readme_said: Open http://localhost:8080. The first visit creates your account.
pitfalls.actually_needed: With no browser, the owner account was made with POST /api/v1/auth/register (from localhost, so no setup code was needed). A token from POST /api/v1/tokens (using the session cookie) was then stored with `ot auth set-token <token> --server <url>`

pitfalls.readme_said: The `ot` command-line client is in the CLI guide
pitfalls.actually_needed: `ot` is a separate release asset (ot-linux-amd64) and has to be downloaded alongside the server binary

pitfalls.readme_said: Single binary: run it; serves on port 8080
pitfalls.actually_needed: Works as stated: the log reads 'opentodo listening addr=:8080 data_dir=./data version=v1.5.0'

judge.observed: All three checks exit 0 with their expected signals: the natural-language add returns JSON with title "Call Sarah", the script output includes "estimate_minutes":90 plus a task list row, and the version prints "ot v1.5.0".

features.feature: quick add tasks in natural language
plan the day with time blocking
features.note: its check passed, but the output does not show it: Output only shows a task with an estimate and a due time, with no Day/Week calendar scheduling or time block shown.

what_it_does.quote: OpenTodo is a free, open-source to-do app you run on your own server or have hosted for you. It works on your phone and your computer, even offline, shares lists with your family or your team

who_it_is_for.quote: Share a project with your family or your team as viewer, editor or admin.

prerequisites.quote: To build from source: `make build && ./bin/opentodo` (Go 1.26+ and Node 22+).

first_run_example.quote: Open <http://localhost:8080>. The first visit creates your account. No configuration needed.

config_and_keys.quote: Nothing is required. Every setting is an optional environment variable with a safe default

troubleshooting_uninstall.quote: Replace the image or the binary and restart; back up first.

license_and_platforms.quote: Download `opentodo-<os>-<arch>` for Linux, macOS or Windows from the [latest release]

evidence.quote: An open-source, local-first task manager you can host yourself.
The first visit creates your account. No configuration needed.
